correctness.rationale: The normalized conditional stationary Fourier equations reconstruct the known characteristic function, including both one-half switching-state probabilities. The Frullani identity gives the exact positive Lévy measure and the finite-activity component of mass \(\log 2\). The explicit profile \(k(r)\) is nonincreasing for every radius iff \(\alpha\ge 2(\sqrt2-1)\); below it the profile increases close to zero. In the upper regime direct integration of \(-k'\) gives the jump rate \(\alpha\), and OU convolution yields exactly \(k(r)/r\); in the lower regime canonical class-L necessity rules out every scalar linear Lévy OU stationary representation. Quantifiers are all \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\); the equality case is included. Executed quadrature and simulations are consistency checks, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Frydel's physical model has an exact non-Gaussian stationary law previously described via Gaussian mixtures and an as-yet-unspecified independent process. The theorem builds explicit independent Lévy and OU surrogates and proves a sharp physical switching-rate distinction: all laws are ID but low-rate laws are not attainable by any constant-rate Lévy OU, while upper-rate laws are and have jump dynamics of rate \(\alpha\). Both a fixed \(\log 2\) finite-activity split and an explicit model-specific boundary give structural content beyond substituting names into a classical theorem. It deliberately does not assert process-level equality.
